chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Dressing in the boiler room and Bill Robinson's objection
summary: They dressed with Frank Mills' band in the boiler room; Robinson said they should refuse, but Bubbles let it go.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Now, when I come off, I don't want to talk to the stage manager, he done made me -- look, I'm so mad enough on what he said to me that I don't want to even talk to him. I passed by him and go on down stage -- took one bow and went on downstairs. We dressed in the boiler room, you know where Frank Mills band -- they were dressing in the same room. There were a couple of acts dressing in the same room down there in the boiler room, you know. But Bill Robinson, he didn't want to dress in that room, he said we shouldn't dress in it. Yeah, but I

knew the public don't know that we're not going to be in the "Follies" on account of our dressing room. We're not going to show our dressing room on the stage. We're going to show ourselves on the stage. So dressing room is a bad policy, but I ain't going to worry about that. I'm just going to try to do the act. So he didn't get me to quit or argue with Ziegfeld about the dressing room. I let that slide, 'cause he wanted me to fix it so it would be easier for him to get in the show if we get out. 'Cause he's the only thing left.
